title: The effectiveness and safety of high-intensity interval training, yoga and intermittent hypoxia-hyperoxia exposure on cognitive performance and health in individuals with mild cognitive impairment: a randomized, sham-controlled trial
summary: The most common illnesses occurring after the age of 60 are diseases in which the brain no longer functions properly – particularly with regard to thinking, remembering, and understanding (= neurocognitive disorders). Dementia is one example. Ensuring optimal care and social participation for people with dementia places high demands on the healthcare system and society. Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) can be a precursor to dementia. In MCI, for example, initial memory problems may appear, but without yet significantly impacting daily life. This is a critical window, as in some affected individuals, MCI develops into dementia within five years. A diagnosis of MCI offers opportunities for the early prevention of subsequent severe cognitive or dementia-related illnesses, as well as possibilities for secondary prevention. As there are currently no medications that can cure MCI or dementia, non-pharmacological therapeutic approaches are a promising option. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness, safety and feasibility of three therapies to be applied twice weekly for 12 weeks: endurance training, yoga and a special breathing therapy involving alternately (intermittent) inhalation of air with low (hypoxia) and high (hyperoxia) oxygen levels. The study will investigate the effect of these therapies on the thinking, physical performance and health of people with MCI compared to a sham application.

interventions.name: High-intensity interval training (HIIT): Participants in the HIIT group perform HIIT twice a week for 12 weeks using a cycle ergometer. Their individual training parameters will be determined based on a baseline spiroergometry test.

Yoga: As part of the yoga intervention, participants attend two group yoga classes per week for 12 weeks. The course includes a combination of postures (asanas), meditation (dhyana) and breathing techniques (panayama), all of which are adapted to suit the target group.

Intermittent hypoxia-hyperoxia exposure (IHHE): Participants receive two IHHE treatments per week using the ReOxy IHHE device (Class IIb medical device, Ai Mediq, Luxembourg) over a period of 12 weeks. The device's algorithm determines the individual treatment parameters based on hypoxia tests.
Control group/sham-IHHE: Participants in the control group will receive two sessions of sham-IHHE per week for 12 weeks under normoxia.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-	MCI (classification according to DemTect < 13 [cut-off for cognitive impairment] and DemTect > 8 [cut-off for no dementia]) 
-	Physical condition that permits the use of a cycle ergometer and participation in the interventions
-	Sufficient time availability (e.g. assessments, intervention)
-	Adequate language, visual, and hearing ability for completion of self-reported and interviewer-administered assessment instruments
-	Ability to travel to the study center
-	Age ≥ 60 years
-	Provision of informed consent and willingness to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
-	Severe psychiatric and neurological disorders (e.g., Parkinson’s disease, Huntington’s disease, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, cerebrovascular disease with acute stroke or cerebral hemorrhage within the past 6 months)
-	Congenital or acquired cardiac and major vascular malformations
-	Renal failure
-	Diagnosed dementia
-	Comorbidities that contraindicate physical exercise, HIIT, Yoga or IHHE (e.g., untreated hypertension, coronary artery disease with unstable angina pectoris [Canadian Cardiovascular Society, CCS grade 3–4], heart failure [New York Heart Association, NYHA class II–IV], myocardial infarction within the past 3 months, pulmonary fibrosis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease [GOLD stage II, FEV₁ < 80% predicted at rest], bronchial asthma with significant dyspnea, oncological diseases, acute inflammatory or somatic diseases) 
-	Abnormal findings during baseline (t0) ergometry that represent a contraindication for HIIT, Yoga or IHHE (e.g., musculoskeletal complaints or clinically relevant ECG or blood pressure abnormalities)
-	Requirement for supplemental oxygen (continuous or intermittent, device-assisted)
-	Resting oxygen saturation < 90%
-	Individual intolerance or hypersensitivity to oxygen
-	Current smoking
-	Alcohol dependence within the past 2 years
-	Multiday stay at altitudes > 1,500 m above sea level within the past 4 weeks
-	Current yoga practice
-	≥ 150 minutes of moderate or ≥ 75 minutes of vigorous physical activity per week (excluding daily activity for transportation purposes)
-	Concurrent participation in another clinical intervention study
